newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica says interest high in unit.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica says interest high in unit.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp cited good interest in its consumer financial unit, Security Pacific Financial Services, which is currently up for sale.
"Interest in that property is high," said chief financial officer Mike O'Neill on a conference call.
Last month, BankAmerica said it planned to sell the unit, with loan assets of $1.4 billion, excluding its executive and professional business uni, which will not be sold.
"A lot of psople are calling and we are mid-stream in that process," O'Neill said. BankAmerica has said it hopes to conclude the deal by the second half of 1997.

He said the planned sale was part of a continuing review of units. "We are just scratching the surface," O'Neill said. "It's not just about exiting businesses. It's also about growing businesses that you can do well in and shrinking the capital that's committed to businesses we don't think we can fix over the long haul."
He said first quarter earnings topped forecasts and cited improvements in many sectors, but said rises in net credit losses and delinquencies were troubling.
"We saw both our net credit losses and delinquenices on cards go up," he said.
"Our increase is less than the industry's but still somewhat troubling," O'Neill said. "Cards as a percentage of our total portfolio is quite small -- about $10 bilion.
"It's something we'll continue to keep a close eye on and the one credit negative in an otherwise strong story."

O'Neill cited especially strong loan growth in California. Asked if BankAmerica picked up some business as a result of Wells Fargo and Co's integration with First Interstate Bancorp, he said, "I don't think their integration process has hurt us."
